🇷🇺 Russian Forces Strike Zaporozhye Infrastructure Russian units launched strikes on key targets in Zaporozhye , including the Dnepr Hydroelectric Station (DneproGES), bridges, and rail facilities. DneproGES: Two jet-powered UAVs hit the plant, causing a fire in the open switchyard and transformer equipment across 150 m². The dam road is currently blocked in both directions. Rail & Industry: A jet UAV struck the internal railway station "Zaporozhstal-Yuzhnaya," damaging a TMU-18 shunting locomotive. Power Grid: An attack on the 330 kV "Zaporozhskaya" substation damaged transmission lines and protective structures. Bridges: The cable-stayed bridge over the Dnepr sustained surface damage to concrete structures. @Slavyangrad

Proving to adversaries that sanctions and pressure on Iran are futile is currently more important than negotiating; however, Tehran has not abandoned the prospect of talks and continues to work in that direction, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said. "Negotiations are part of our work; we have not forgotten about them and continue to engage in them. Yet, under current circumstances, there is an even more important mission: to demonstrate to our enemies that the sanctions and pressure they exert on our country will be ineffective. The negotiation process has its own established mechanism and is conducted under the oversight of the Supreme National Security Council," he said in comments to the Iranian state broadcasting organization.

🇺🇸 📲 How Nvidia’s obsession with Chinese women undermined US chip restrictions Jensen Huang is not the only Nvidia executive to have been romantically involved with a Chinese woman potentially connected to chip smuggling, The Wall Street Journal reports. Jay Puri, a former executive vice president of Nvidia's Worldwide Field Operations, dated Super Micro Computer Senior Executive Cenly Chen for years before marrying her on March 7 this year. Notably, Puri stepped down from his executive position in July but remained a senior adviser. 👉 Chen reportedly leveraged her relationship with Puri to pressure Nvidia into supplying chips to Super Micro customers. During Super Micro sales meetings, she also made it clear to team members that she could fix Nvidia-related issues. Meanwhile, on March 19, the Justice Department charged Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and other individuals with smuggling more than $500 million worth of servers containing high-end Nvidia chips into China. To facilitate the scheme, they reportedly directed an unidentified company in Southeast Asia to place orders for approximately $2.5 billion worth of Super Micro servers in 2024 and 2025. 👉 The FBI has recently been investigating the case and questioning Super Micro executives, including Chen, who has denied being contacted by federal agents. Liaw has pleaded not guilty and resigned from his position. The WSJ reports that Huang and Puri cultivated dozens of business partners in the US and Asia who could have covertly supplied China with high-end chips despite US export restrictions . Some Nvidia customers, including Asia-based Megaspeed, are now in the FBI's crosshairs. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
